subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should core adopt the disabled-by-default maintenance timeout and synchronous queue callback as the permanent resolution for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96703?
rationale: Source review can validate the mechanism, but only feature owners can decide whether an operator-only setting sufficiently fixes the default user experience and whether this new configuration/API surface is preferable to an existing timeout or host-owned default.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in mitigation
options.body: Rebase and merge the current contract, but keep the canonical issue open unless maintainers explicitly accept operator configuration as the complete resolution.

options.title: Define a safe host default
options.body: Choose and prove a default timeout or queued-foreground policy that protects ordinary users while preserving legitimate long-running maintenance upgrades.

options.title: Reuse an existing timeout contract
options.body: Avoid the new key by formally applying the existing compaction timeout semantics to deferred maintenance, with focused compatibility proof.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in mitigation
recommendation.body: Rebase and merge the current contract, but keep the canonical issue open unless maintainers explicitly accept operator configuration as the complete resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the background-maintenance lifecycle whose liveness and compatibility policy is being changed.
